Windows Subsystem for Linux ([WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install)) allows you to run Linux on your Windows computer without a virtual machine or dual-booting. You can use Linux command-line tools and applications alongside your Windows programs.

## Install

Open Windows PowerShell as Administrator and run the following commands: 

```powershell
wsl install 
```

To view a list of available linux distributions (*distro*), run the following:

```powershell
wsl --list --online
```

Pick the distro you'd like to install (i.e., Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, openSUSE, etc.) and install it using (replacing `<distro>` with the name of the distribution): 

```powershell
wsl --install -d <distro>
```

See example below: 

```powershell
wsl --install -d Ubuntu
```
